{ State of North Carolina
{ Comptroller's Office
I, William J. Clarke, Comptroller of public accounts in and for the State aforesaid, do hereby certify that it appears of record in my office among the payments made by said State to sundry persons for Military services in the Revolutionary War, as follows to wit:
John Bostic
Indent or Army Certificate No 321 issued by auditors of the Counties of Montgomery and Anson July 29th. 1782
₤50.S0.D4 specie.
Ditto auditors of Hillsboro' District No. 2354 June 1783 ₤42S5. spec
Treasury Certif. No. 143 ₤22S4D3 specie -
Ditto                 " 214 ₤25 S12 D8  "
Book No. 10 page 27 - ₤7 S19 - "

There also appear payments to "Captain Bostic's Company," but no Christian name is given, and I am unable to determine whether John Bostic was the Captain or not.

[seal]
In testimony whereof I have hereunto subscribed my name and affixed my seal of office this 24th day of May 1853. -
(1853) S/Wm J. Clarke, Compt'r.

<image>
Transcribe this page, one line of text per written line.

{Printed document with handwritten entries, and lines crossed out]

WAR DEPARTMENT.
REVOLUTIONARY CLAIM.

I certify that, in conformity with [Crossed out: the 3rd section of] the law of the United States, of the 7th of June 1832 Jesse Wood, deceased, who was a private, was entitled to a pension the rate of Twenty dollars per ann. coming on the 4th of March, 1831, and ending
on the 17th of June, 1836, the day of his death, which will be paid upon the production of the proper vouchers, to Nancy Wood, his widow.

[Lines crossed out]

Given at the War Office of the United States, this - 18th- day of October, one thousand eight hundred and forty-five-

Payable at Richmond, Virginia.

Secretary of War.

Examined and Countersigned.}

Commissioner of Pensions.
